newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada rejects call for more inflation.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada rejects call for more inflation.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Wednesday he does not agree with recent proposals to raise inflation-control targets in Canada.
"I certainly do not agree with the proposal to relax our inflation-control targets," he told a group of businessmen.
Thiessen said that recent interest rate cuts will inevitably spur a rise in consumer spending.

"I believe that it is only a matter of time before this monetary easing encourages a resurgence in household spending. Indeed some indicators of consumer and housing activity have a more positive tone to them," he said.
Thiessen said he has heard no arguments to convince him that changing recent economic policies will bring benefits.

"Let me say that I have heard no persuasive arguments for changing the economic policies that have helped to bring about the recent improvements in the foundation of our economy. Certainly any sign of a reversal in monetary policy could quickly undo some of these improvements," he said.
"I am convinced that the Canadian economy is on the right path," he said.
Some economists have recently called for a relaxation in inflation targets as a means of spurring employment growth.
But Thiessen said he does not agree that more inflation is needed as a lubricant for the economy and Canadians will soon see the benefits of a low inflation policy on the economy.
"The economic outlook is favorable. We will soon see signs of the payoff for the difficult restructuring decisions taken in both the private and public sectors," Thiessen said.
